encounters.cc: New tender breast lump discovered on self-examination two weeks ago with cyclical lump history.

lines: New tender breast lump discovered on self-examination two weeks ago with cyclical lump history.

The patient is a 30-year-old female with established generalized anxiety disorder, beta-thalassemia minor, fibrocystic breast changes, and chronic insomnia disorder who presents with a new breast concern.
She returns to the outpatient setting approximately one year following her preconception counseling encounter, reporting symptoms in the context of her known fibrocystic breast changes.
She reports that she first noticed the lump approximately 2 weeks ago, and it has gradually become more tender over the past several days.
She also indicates that she frequently develops smaller breast lumps that seem to appear and disappear in relation to her menstrual cycle.
She notes that in the past, these lumps have caused discomfort before her period and then diminished or resolved once menstruation began.
She recalls that during her last two cycles she noticed similar nodules, which worried her initially, but they went away as soon as her period started.
Her menses occur at regular 28-day intervals.
Her last menstrual period was approximately 3 weeks ago.
She describes her breasts as feeling "lumpy and achy" every month, especially in the days leading up to her period.
She often needs to wear a more supportive bra during that time to help with discomfort.
She states that she has become increasingly anxious because this new lump feels larger than the ones she has felt before.
She indicates that she has read online that breast pain and nodules can sometimes be signs of cancer, which has caused her significant worry.
- Insomnia - indication for pharmacologic therapy with Z-drugs (diagnosed 2020-04-15)
She has never had breast trauma or prior breast surgery.
- Zolpidem 5 mg orally at bedtime PRN insomnia (limited to 10 tablets/month)
She has no family history of breast or ovarian cancer.
She does not smoke, drinks alcohol only occasionally, and exercises several times a week.
She eats a balanced diet, has a normal body mass index.
She denies nipple discharge, skin dimpling, fever, or systemic symptoms.
On examination, her vital signs are normal.
There is no lymphadenopathy in the cervical, supraclavicular, or axillary regions.
The breasts are symmetric with no overlying skin changes such as dimpling, erythema, or peau d’orange.
Palpation of the right breast reveals multiple small, smooth, soft, mobile nodules clustered in the upper outer quadrant, the largest measuring about 2 cm.
The nodules are mildly tender to palpation but not associated with overlying warmth.
The left breast also contains several smaller, mobile nodules with similar characteristics.
Both breasts are diffusely tender to deep palpation, particularly in the upper outer quadrants.
There is no nipple retraction or abnormal discharge.
The masses are mobile, not fixed, and there is no evidence of overlying erythema, warmth, or fluctuation.
No discrete dominant mass is palpated, but the tissue feels more nodular than expected for her age.
